title: Work Done by a Force

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Work, Energy and Power

explanation: Work done by a constant force equals the product of the force magnitude, the displacement magnitude, and the cosine of the angle between them — only the component of force ALONG the displacement direction contributes. Work is a scalar (dot product of two vectors), and can be positive (force helps motion), negative (force opposes motion, e.g. friction), or zero (force perpendicular to displacement, e.g. gravity on a horizontally moving object, or no displacement at all).

variables.meaning: Angle between force and displacement vectors

workedExample.scenario: A 20 N force pulls a box 5 m along the ground at an angle of 60° to the ground.

commonMistakes: Forgetting the cosθ factor and just multiplying F×d, ignoring the angle between force and displacement.
Assuming work is always positive — a force acting opposite to displacement (like friction) does NEGATIVE work.
Believing a force does work even with zero displacement — holding a heavy object stationary does zero work in the physics sense, however tiring it feels.
genZNote: No displacement, no work — physics doesn't care how tired your arms are.
